text:
Vancouver is 3-17-1, last in the league, with seven points: the worst 20-game start in franchise history, by the club's own count, and it's now 21 games. The loss to the Rangers on Friday was the seventh straight, and the Canucks haven't won at home since October 3. Our numbers put their playoff chances at zero.

This was supposed to be a patient year. Daniel and Henrik Sedin took over hockey operations in May, Ryan Johnson became general manager, and Manny Malhotra got his first head coaching job. The Sedins said this week they're unhappy, they trust Malhotra, and they won't sell players cheaply for picks.

The results are not bad luck. Vancouver has 40% of the expected goals, the worst kind of number, and has allowed 15 more goals than even those chances predicted. With Thatcher Demko out and no timeline, Kevin Lankinen has stopped 80% of shots over his last five starts, 9.3 goals worse than expected. Filip Hronek and the defenseman Elias Pettersson (38% of the expected goals) have been buried.

Something to hold onto: the first line with Elias Pettersson, Jake DeBrusk and Brock Boeser is close to even. Filip Chytil and Tom Willander returned on Friday. What we'd watch now is whether the work holds up through December, because the standings already decided the season.
headline: The Canucks have hit the bottom
